title: bn254-gt-dlp: gated tag-tracing rho with a generated 217-instruction step loop and lazy window product, expected work 2^119.68

claims.statement: For uniform z=g^x in the protected BN254 GT (g=e(P0,Q0) from target-profile.json, x uniform in [0,r)), the gated tag-tracing 8-adding distinguished-point Pollard rho of proof.md (a point Y is distinguished iff t(Y) 2^84 < p, the same 84-bit predicate in the algorithm, the caps and the ledger) returns x with g^x=z with probability at least 0.39 over uniform challenges and fresh coins, at EXPECTED total work at most 1 + (K/2^64)(217 E[T] + 9216 (E[T]/256 + E[walks] + 1) + 2^110)/20000 < 2^119.68 reference units (W=R/20,000, R total scalar AArch64 instruction-equivalent work). This is an expectation over the challenge and the coins of the one attack on the one target, not a bound on every run; every run, including all failures, is capped at 2^126.70 units by a 2^133-step global three-word step counter, at most 2^52 walks of at most 2^90 steps, at most 2^90 exact evaluations, at most 2^70 store probes and at most 1,024 draws per random scalar. The attack first draws a fresh uniform 64-bit word v and stops as a failure unless v < K = 7416732153347139310, the least K with (K/2^64) x 0.97 >= 0.39; past the gate it runs to its first verified recovery and succeeds with probability at least 0.9760 (failure budget below 0.0240: step cap at most 0.019115 by Markov's inequality, walk cap at most 0.004779, all other caps and degenerate events below 2^-16). The walk Y -> Y*M_s with s = floor(8t/p) for the protected-basis constant coefficient t, the tag certificate (proved), the 525,783,425,977,953-entry table of all products of at most 256 multipliers are those of submission 73463878-0c19-4309-a991-749ea525d51c, whose reference.py, experiment.py, listings and development evidence are included byte for byte except DP_BITS = 84 in experiment.py and the dbits=84 docstring in reference.py; the gate and run-to-collision expected-work accounting follow submission 8b901b3d-a617-4b1f-a442-ff370e6ec4f7. New here: a generated step loop of 217 executed scalar AArch64 instructions per certified step (lazy.py part S: same tag sum, certificate test and pointer walk as the base listing ttstep.disasm.txt of 273, encoding-validated and executed trip by trip against the definition with all three exits exercised); the window re-base uses a generated straight-line lazy-reduction Fp12 product of 8,679 scalar AArch64 instructions, encoding-validated and executed instruction by instruction on a simulator against big-integer arithmetic (lazy.py part L), so a window end costs at most 9,216 instructions and a step 217 + 9216/256 = 253 instructions; the tag certificate is re-checked in this layout on window bases produced by that routine (part T), and a 120-step full-width walk on real table entries (window length 8 in the test) runs through both generated programs with 14 window ends and 0 mismatches (part I). The expected work uses E[T] <= 1.05 sqrt(pi kappa r/2) + 2^85 <= 2^127.2909 steps, kappa = 8/7 (premise H-mean on the mean collision time of the 8-adding walk, with H1 and H2 of the base package), supported by toy-scale runs of the complete walk (lazy.py part H and development-evidence-mean.json: offline per-setting means 0.927 to 0.996 of the model at 16 to 32 bits) and extrapolated to production size. Table construction (below 2^69 instructions) and all other work are included without amortization. Peak storage is below 2^62 bytes, nonuniform advice 0 bytes. No production-size run is claimed; this is a generic square-root attack, not a security estimate.

experiments.purpose: Part C: assert that submission.json, proof.md and machine.md state one 84-bit distinguished-point predicate, the same parameters as the code, and rounded bounds on the safe side of the ledger. Part S: generate the tag-tracing step loop, validate the encoding of every instruction and execute it trip by trip on synthetic table entries against the definition (A, selector, child, exits). Part L: generate the lazy-reduction window-end Fp12 product as a straight-line scalar AArch64 program with asserted static bounds, validate the encoding of every instruction, execute it on an instruction simulator and compare with big-integer arithmetic. Part T: check the tag certificate in this layout on window bases produced by that routine. Part H: toy-scale runs of the complete 8-adding distinguished-point walk run to recovery, mean collision time against sqrt(pi kappa n/2). Part I: a full-width walk on real table entries through both generated programs, checked step by step against the definition. Part X (declared input only): assert that every experimental figure stated in the manifest, proof.md and machine.md equals this run's measured value. Part G: gate, caps, failure budget and expected-work ledger in exact decimal arithmetic. Then execute the base package's experiment.py (submission 73463878; changed only to DP_BITS = 84) in-process: tower and row checks, tag certificate on 260 cases, 120-step full-width walk (steps_wanted = 120), toy runs at the cap, listing recount. Toy runs are evidence at their own scale only.
